Dyes such as Congo red are often found in industrial
wastewater and must be removed before the water can be
discharged. Scientists performed 3 experiments to deter-
mine how much Congo red would be removed from a solu-
tion by binding to particles of bentonite (B), which is a
type of clay, or to particles of a chemically modified ben-
In each trial of each experiment, Steps 1
1. A 50 mL volume of an aqueous 300 mg/L Congo red
solution having a particular pH was placed in each of
2 flasks. A specific mass of B was added to one flask,
and the same mass of MB was added to the other flask.
2. The flasks were sealed and shaken at a speed of 200 rev-
olutions per minute for a certain length of time at 25°C.
3. The contents of each flask were filtered to remove all
4. The concentration of Congo red remaining in the solu-
tion from each flask was measured.
5. The percent of Congo red that had been removed (% CR
removed) from the solution was calculated for each
In all trials, the pH of the Congo red solution was the
same, and the shaking time was 360 min. From trial to
trial, the mass of B and of MB was varied. The results are
In all trials, the mass of B and of MB was 0.100 g, and

In all trials, the pH of the Congo red solution was the
